I'm working out a rule for classifying objects: color 1 if size equals height+width-1 (a path spanning the bounding box), color 6 if the object matches its box outline exactly, otherwise color 2. Checking object A with 8 cells in a 3x5 box, its size doesn't match the height+width-1 formula so it doesn't get color 1.

Object A also has interior cells not on the box outline, so it gets color 2. Object B similarly fails both checks and gets color 2, while Object C has size matching height+width-1 exactly, giving it color 1. Objects D and E both have interior cells breaking the box-outline match, so they also get color 2, and I'm now checking Object F's cells against the same criteria.

content.text:
I'm working out the classification rule: single-corner L-shapes map to blue, shapes matching a specific outline pattern map to pink, and everything else maps to red. Now I'm sketching out test grids containing L-shapes, U/Z-shapes with two corners, and three-corner shapes to verify this rule.

I'm running into a snag though — the size formula (h+w-1) that should distinguish an L-shape can also match certain Z-shaped staircases, which breaks my assumption that it only captures single-corner shapes. So I decide to test cautiously against actual tool outputs rather than trust my own derivation, and start constructing a three-corner shape example to check against the real answer.

Confirming that shape has an interior cell off the bounding box border, meaning it should classify as red. So I settle on the rule: red shapes have interior cells outside the box's border, while blue and pink follow the earlier size-based conditions.

Now I'm laying out an 11x11 grid with an L-shape (blue) in one corner, a U-shape (pink) alongside it, and I'm starting to place a T/cross shape with an interior cell to represent red.

This makes the interior cell (7,7) filled and red as intended. I'll apply similar varied shapes for Grid B and Grid C.
